text: {"facts":[{"statement":"The task is to find a minimum-cost concatenation of dictionary words covering the text; words may be reused, and duplicate entries may have different costs.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"The text length is at most 100000, there are at most 2000 dictionary entries, each word has length 1 to 30, and costs are nonnegative and at most 1000000000.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"The required output is the minimum cost, or -1 if no cover exists.","source_ids":["task"]},{"statement":"The first public example expects output 3 for text \"b\".","source_ids":["public1"]},{"statement":"The second public example expects output -1 for text \"bbaaaa\".","source_ids":["public2"]}],"open_requirements":["Produce a complete Python 3.11 program using only the standard library, reading the specified input format and writing the required output.","Choose an algorithm that handles the input limits and duplicate words with different costs correctly."],"tentative_options":[{"id":"ac-dp","method":"Build an Aho–Corasick matcher for dictionary words, then use dynamic programming over text positions to minimize cost for each word match.","unverified_assumptions":["The implementation can process all matches within acceptable time and memory for the stated limits."]},{"id":"bounded-lookback-dp","method":"Use dynamic programming over text positions and inspect candidate word lengths up to 30, matching dictionary entries through a suitable lookup structure.","unverified_assumptions":["The chosen lookup structure keeps the total work feasible for up to 2000 entries and 100000 text characters."]}],"possible_checks":["Test that each supplied public example produces its stated output.","Test a text covered by multiple entries for the same word with different costs, verifying that the cheaper cost is used.","Test an uncovered text and a cover that reuses a dictionary word."]}
